claims.claim_ar: تكرار لفظة «الأسماء» (الأَسْمَاءُ ... أَسْمَائِهِ) كوسيلة بلاغية لتأكيد خصوصية الأسماء الحسنى وإثارتها عند السامع.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the word “al-asmā’” (al-asmaa ... asma'ihi) as a rhetorical device to emphasize the particularity and importance of the Beautiful Names.

claims.claim_ar: طباق/مقابلة بين الأمر بالدعاء بالأسماء الحسنى (فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا) وبين الأمر بترك الذين يُلْحِدُونَ فِي أَسْمَائِهِ — أي مقابلتان: فعل التقرّب بالاسم مقابل إعراض المخالفين، لبيان التباين في الموقف والعقاب.
claims.claim_en: Tibaq/muqabalah (antithesis) between the command to invoke God by His Beautiful Names (fa-ud'ūhu bihā) and the command to leave those who deviate in His names — a contrast between drawing near (by invocation) and turning away (and the sinners' recompense), highlighting difference in stance and consequence.
claims.needs_review_reason: Identification as tibaq/muqabalah is interpretive (contrast between clauses). Support cited discusses 'طباق' generally but does not analyze this exact ayah; recommend corroboration from a balagha commentary explicitly noting the antithesis here.

claims.claim_ar: التفات بلاغي في التنقل من صيغة الأمر المباشر (فَادْعُوهُ بِهَا) إلى توجيه ترك المخالفين ثم إلى البيان التحذيري بالمستقبل (سَيُجْزَوْنَ) — أي تغيير أسلوبي ولغوي يلفت نظر السامع ويؤكد الجزاء.
claims.claim_en: Iltifat (shift): a rhetorical shift from direct imperative (fa-ud'ūhu bihā) to the injunction to abandon the deviators and then to a future indicative warning (they will be recompensed), creating a stylistic move that attracts attention and stresses the retribution.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited source phrase concerns rhetorical 'التعرّض' but is not an explicit commentary tying this ayah to 'التفات'. The classification as iltifat is plausible but requires confirmation from an explicit balagha source that analyzes this verse's shift in address/structure.

warnings: Provided source_chunks are excerpts from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) only. The developer instruction requested authors like al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Bāqillānī, al-Suyūṭī, and tafsir-balagha materials; such explicit sources were not provided. Claims therefore use the available chunks as supporting quotations and some identifications (especially structural labels like 'iltifat' or 'tibaq') are interpretive and flagged for review.
